summary: The game has a severe difficulty cliff: casual, learner, and turtle players quit at 78-97% rates and win only 6-15% of rounds, while cheesers exploit a dominant SWEEP/GROUND strategy to win 92% with 6% quit. Round 2 is a massive frustration wall (31% overall quit rate, 50-75% for weak archetypes). A physics bug (!airborne) appears on turtle and explorer runs, and masher/learner show zero progression — win rates flatline across rounds. (Verification: 0 of 31 claims did not match the recomputed value; 13 cited seeds did not exist in the runs and were removed.)

findings.title: Casual/learner/turtle hit a difficulty wall at Round 2 and quit en masse
findings.narrative: Round 2 quit rates are catastrophic for weak archetypes: casual 59%, learner 27%, turtle 5%, masher 50%, rusher 35%. Overall 31% of players quit right after Round 2. These archetypes also have win rates of 4-8% in Round 2 and 0-5% in Round 3, meaning they cannot progress. The session end reasons confirm this: 708 frustration quits vs only 250 satisfied.

seeds.why: casual quits after R2 frustration, 0% win rate

findings.suggestion: Add a difficulty ramp: reduce rival aggression/HP in Rounds 1-2, or give players a defensive tool (parry/dodge) that works at low skill.

findings.title: Cheeser archetype exploits SWEEP/GROUND spam for 92% win rate and near-zero frustration
findings.narrative: Cheesers (100 players, 299 rounds) win 92% overall with only 6% quit rate and 7% koShare. They land SWEEP (3538 total events) and GROUND (2526) at massive volume while taking minimal damage (meanHpLoss 48.1 vs 85.9 overall). Their strategy is repeatable: SWEEP x3-6 + GROUND x1-4 per round, often winning in 15-20s. No other archetype approaches this win rate.
findings.suggestion: Nerf SWEEP/GROUND frame advantage or add rival counter-play (armor/parry vs low attacks). Require move variety for full damage.

findings.title: Physics bug: !airborne invariant violation on turtle and explorer players
findings.narrative: Multiple turtle and explorer rounds show '!airborne@<time>' events, marking engine invariant violations. Examples: p0009 R3 (!airborne@16.6), p0114 R3 (!airborne@18.0), p0254 R1 (!airborne@11.1), p0745 R3 (!airborne@13.2), p0355 R2 (!airborne@16.6). These correlate with high frustration and KO losses. The bug likely causes unfair knockdowns or state desync.
findings.suggestion: Fix the airborne state invariant — likely a collision/grounding check that fails on certain move sequences. Add automated regression test for !airborne.

findings.title: Rusher archetype is the only non-cheeser with viable win rate (42%) but still quits 72%
findings.narrative: Rushers (160 players) win 42% overall — second best after cheesers — but 72% still quit (mostly frustration). They win early (R1 44%, R2 38%) but quit spikes at R2 (35%) and R3 (46%). Their style (BODY_JAB, ROUNDHOUSE_KICK, GROUND) works but feels unrewarding. They need a satisfaction hook: visible progress, combo variety, or less HP loss on wins (meanHpLoss 82.9).

seeds.why: rusher wins R1-R4, quits R5 frustration

findings.suggestion: Add rusher-friendly rewards: meter gain on aggression, visible combo counter, or reduce HP loss on successful rushdowns.

findings.title: Speedrunner and explorer have polarized outcomes — either dominate or quit fast
findings.narrative: Speedrunners (60 players) win 65% but 28% quit; explorers (80 players) win 32% with 60% quit. Both have low avgDuration (9.8s, 12.1s) meaning rounds end fast — either quick KOs or quick deaths. Speedrunners use GROUND/ROUNDHOUSE_KICK/PUNCH combos; explorers mix JAB/SWEEP/ROUNDHOUSE_KICK. The variance suggests matchup RNG or seed sensitivity, not skill expression.
findings.suggestion: Reduce round-ending volatility: increase HP pools, add comeback mechanics, or make KO require combo/confirmation not single big hit.

findings.title: Turtle archetype is a trap — high patience but 11% win rate, 89% KO share, 78% quit
findings.narrative: Turtles (120 players) have high patience (avg 0.8+) and frustration tolerance but get crushed: 11% win rate, 89% koShare, 96.6 meanHpLoss. They block/parry (blk 1-5, par 1-4 per round) but it doesn't convert to offense. They quit late (R3 25%, R4 52%, R5 46%) after prolonged suffering. The defensive playstyle is non-viable.
findings.suggestion: Give turtles a counter-attack mechanic: successful block/parry grants guaranteed punish window or meter. Make defense rewarding.

findings.title: Round 3+ survival bias inflates win rates — only strong players remain
findings.narrative: Win rates appear to improve in later rounds (overall R4 40%, R5 45%) but this is survivorship bias: only 253 players reach R4, 92 reach R5. The weak archetypes (casual, learner, turtle) are nearly extinct by R4. Real win rates for the original population stay flat. This masks the difficulty cliff in aggregate metrics.

seeds.why: rusher reaches R5, quits after loss

findings.suggestion: Report cohort-based win rates (of 1000 starters) not conditional-on-reaching-round. Add early-game telemetry to catch the cliff.
